artifacts.location: HKLM\SOFTWARE{\Wow6432Node}\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\<executable>\Debugger; AppInit_DLLs at HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows
artifacts.purpose: IFEO Debugger value causes a specified debugger/program to launch in place of (or before) the target executable; AppInit_DLLs forces a DLL to load into every process that loads user32.dll.
key_fields: Debugger value under an executable's IFEO key
SilentProcessExit\MonitorProcess value
AppInit_DLLs value list
artifacts.normal_baseline: IFEO keys typically empty or used only by legitimate debugging/compatibility tooling; AppInit_DLLs typically empty on modern systems (deprecated with secure boot).
anomalies: Debugger value attached to an accessibility or security-tool binary (e.g. utilman.exe, taskmgr.exe)
AppInit_DLLs pointing to an unsigned DLL in a user-writable path
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: IFEO abuse can double as defense evasion by attaching an invalid or crashing debugger to security tools, silently disabling them.

artifacts.name: Run / RunOnce Registry Keys
artifacts.purpose: Machine-wide or per-user autostart mechanism executing listed commands at logon/boot.
key_fields: Value name
Command/executable path
Key (machine vs. user)
artifacts.normal_baseline: Entries match known startup agents (AV, cloud sync clients, drivers).
anomalies: Entry pointing to a script interpreter with an encoded argument
New entry in a user-writable path added outside a software install event
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: Trivially removed by deleting the value; correlate against SOFTWARE/NTUSER.DAT hive backups (RegBack) to detect since-deleted entries.

artifacts.name: Scheduled Tasks
artifacts.os_min: Windows Vista (XML tasks); legacy .job on XP
artifacts.location: C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\<TaskName> (XML); registry mirror at HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tree and \Tasks
artifacts.purpose: Defines actions executed on a schedule or trigger (logon, event, time); a common legitimate and malicious persistence mechanism.
key_fields: Action command/arguments
Trigger definition
Author/principal (execution context)
Task creation/last-run time
artifacts.normal_baseline: Tasks correspond to installed software's update/maintenance routines and OS-native scheduled maintenance.
anomalies: Action node pointing to Temp/AppData with base64-encoded PowerShell arguments
Suspicious repetition interval (e.g. every few minutes)
Task registered without a corresponding Security 4698 event, suggesting log gaps or non-standard creation (e.g. direct XML drop)
parsing_tools: TaskScheduler view + PECmd/Registry Explorer for TaskCache
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: TaskCache registry entries can persist under \Tasks\{GUID} even after the XML file is deleted, useful for timeline reconstruction. Event IDs 4698/4699 require Object Access auditing to be enabled, which many environments lack by default.

artifacts.name: Windows Services (Persistence)
artifacts.purpose: Services configured with Start=2 (auto) or 3 (demand) launch at boot or on demand, commonly abused for SYSTEM-level persistence.
key_fields: ImagePath
Start type
ServiceDll (for svchost-hosted services)
ObjectName (run-as account)
artifacts.normal_baseline: Services correspond to installed hardware drivers and legitimate software.
anomalies: ImagePath pointing to a non-standard directory
svchost-hosted service with an unrecognized ServiceDll
Service created shortly before/after other IOC timestamps
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: Services can be created/deleted quickly with sc.exe; correlate with Security event 4697/7045 (System log) for creation evidence when auditing is enabled.

artifacts.name: Startup Folders
artifacts.purpose: Any shortcut or executable placed here launches automatically at user logon.
key_fields: File/shortcut name
Target path (if LNK)
Creation/modification timestamp of the item
artifacts.normal_baseline: Contains only shortcuts placed by legitimate software installers.
anomalies: Unrecognized script or executable dropped directly into the folder
LNK target pointing to a scripting interpreter with suspicious arguments
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: Trivially removed by deleting the file; file-system timestamps on the item itself (not just its LNK target) can help date when persistence was planted.

artifacts.name: WMI Permanent Event Subscription
artifacts.os_min: Windows XP (WMI infrastructure); technique common from Windows 7+
artifacts.purpose: Lets code execute automatically when a defined WMI event occurs (e.g. process start, time, logon), providing fileless, reboot-surviving persistence.
key_fields: __EventFilter (Query, QueryLanguage - WQL)
__EventConsumer (CommandLineTemplate or ScriptText)
__FilterToConsumerBinding (links filter to consumer)
artifacts.normal_baseline: Subscriptions correspond to known monitoring/management software (SCCM, AV agents); a subscription is only active when filter, consumer, and binding all exist.
anomalies: CommandLineEventConsumer or ActiveScriptEventConsumer with an unrecognized command or obfuscated script
wmic.exe or mofcomp.exe process creating filter/consumer objects
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: Leaves no on-disk executable if using a script consumer, making it a favored fileless technique; corroborate with Microsoft-Windows-WMI-Activity/Operational Event ID 5861 and Sysmon Event IDs 19/20/21 for a live-log view of when it was installed or fired.

artifacts.name: Browser Downloads History and Session Restore
artifacts.location: Chrome/Edge: History.downloads table in the profile folder; Firefox: downloads recorded via moz_annos in places.sqlite (or separate downloads.sqlite on older versions)
artifacts.purpose: Records files downloaded through the browser (source URL, save path, timestamp) and, via session-restore files, the set of tabs/windows open at last shutdown or crash.
key_fields: Download source URL
Local save path
Download start/end time
Session-restore tab URLs
artifacts.normal_baseline: Downloads correspond to work-related documents/installers from known sources.
anomalies: Download from a known malicious-tool distribution site or file-sharing service immediately preceding execution evidence for the same file
Session-restore tabs referencing an exfiltration or C2 panel URL
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: Downloads table entries can be cleared alongside general history clearing; the downloaded file itself, if kept, will separately carry Zone.Identifier MOTW evidence of its origin.

artifacts.name: Browser Extension IDs / Manifests
artifacts.location: Chrome/Edge: User Data\Default\Extensions\<extension-id>\<version>\manifest.json; Preferences JSON also lists installed extension IDs
artifacts.purpose: Identifies browser extensions installed for a profile, including sideloaded/unpacked extensions not from an official store.
key_fields: Extension ID
manifest.json (name, permissions, version)
Install source (webstore vs. unpacked)
artifacts.normal_baseline: Extension list matches the organization's approved/allow-listed set.
anomalies: Unpacked/developer-mode extension with broad host permissions (e.g. <all_urls>)
Extension ID not present in the official store, suggesting sideloading for credential theft or session hijacking
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: Removing an extension deletes its folder; the Preferences JSON's extension history or sync data may retain remnants briefly after removal.

artifacts.name: Chrome / Edge (Chromium) Browser Artifacts
artifacts.location: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default (Chrome) or \Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default (Edge); History, Login Data, Web Data, Cookies (under Network\), Bookmarks, Preferences
artifacts.purpose: SQLite databases and JSON files recording browsing history, downloads, saved logins, autofill, and cookies.
key_fields: History.urls / History.downloads tables
Login Data.logins table
Web Data.autofill table
Cookies (Network\Cookies) table
artifacts.normal_baseline: History reflects normal work-related browsing; Login Data contains credentials for known, approved services.
anomalies: History entries for known malicious-tool download sites or paste sites shortly before an incident
Downloads entry for a payload matching a known hash
Unexpected extension IDs not present in the organization's approved list
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: Clearing browsing history removes rows from the SQLite tables but does not necessarily overwrite the underlying file pages, so carving deleted SQLite records can sometimes recover cleared history.

artifacts.name: Firefox Browser Artifacts
artifacts.location: C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\<profile>\ ; places.sqlite (history/bookmarks), cookies.sqlite, formhistory.sqlite, logins.json + key4.db (saved passwords)
artifacts.purpose: Stores browsing history, bookmarks, cookies, form autofill history, and encrypted saved logins in per-profile SQLite/JSON files.
key_fields: moz_places / moz_historyvisits tables (URL, visit_date, visit_count)
moz_bookmarks
logins.json encrypted credential entries
artifacts.normal_baseline: History reflects normal work-related browsing patterns for the profile owner.
anomalies: History entries for malicious-tool or paste-site domains
A profile folder present with no corresponding profiles.ini entry, suggesting a portable/hidden profile
artifacts.anti_forensic_notes: Deleting the whole profile folder removes all Firefox artifacts at once; profile folder can be copied off intact even after the browser is closed, as recommended by Mozilla for backups.
